0.long_answer: Laryngeal papillomatosis is a benign condition caused by human papillomavirus (typically types 6 and 11) that results in the formation of squamous cell papillomas on the laryngeal mucosa. These benign tumors commonly develop on areas where the larynx is lined by stratified squamous epithelium, most notably on the true vocal cords, often near the anterior commissure. They can also extend to adjacent regions such as the false vocal cords or supraglottic areas, but the true vocal cords remain the predominant and most frequently involved site.
